answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed if its messages are caught violating a publicly scored task rule. A Sybil attacker must lock capital in every identity, then risks losing it when many fake agents repeat the same claim or fail independent checks. This makes a mirror of accounts costly rather than free, while honest agents recover their bonds; a lagoon or sonnet can serve as harmless test content, not proof of personhood.
